props.title: The Killers
props.initialSlug: Insurance investigator hunts femme fatale's deadly past

sections.content: **The Killers** (1946) revolutionized film noir with its groundbreaking non-linear structure and fatalistic tone. Based on Ernest Hemingway's short story, Robert Siodmak's masterpiece opens with one of noir's most chilling sequences - two hitmen methodically terrorizing a diner before killing the Swede (Burt Lancaster in his film debut). The investigation into why he accepted death so passively unfolds through multiple perspectives, predating **Rashomon** (1950) in its innovative storytelling. Lancaster's haunting performance as the doomed ex-boxer and Ava Gardner's quintessential femme fatale created the template for countless noir films to follow.

sections.content: Siodmak's visual style in **The Killers** (1946) exemplifies German Expressionist influence on noir, with stark shadows, canted angles, and oppressive urban landscapes. The film's influence extends directly to later neo-noir classics like **Point Blank** (1967) and **Drive** (2011), which echo its themes of masculine fatalism and betrayal. The innovative flashback structure influenced **Pulp Fiction** (1994) and countless modern crime films.

The film's treatment of masculinity in crisis became a noir hallmark. Lancaster's Swede represents the damaged post-war male - physically powerful but emotionally vulnerable. This theme resonates through later films like **The Set-Up** (1949) and **On the Waterfront** (1954), where boxers and dock workers struggle with similar existential threats to their masculine identity. sections.content: **The Killers** (1946) spawned two remakes - Don Siegel's brutal 1964 version with Lee Marvin and a 1956 student film by Andrei Tarkovsky. The original's DNA appears in everything from **Reservoir Dogs** (1992) to **No Country for Old Men** (2007), particularly in their cold-blooded professional killers and deterministic worldview. The film's opening sequence directly inspired **Blue Velvet** (1986) and countless other neo-noirs.
